title: GROVE emissions are permanently disabled beyond genesis, but Sky Governance keeps a Risk-Capital override that Grove itself can never use
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.2.1.1.6 sets up a one-way valve: "Token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are permanently disabled; this cannot be reverted by Grove Governance. Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Grove is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework."

This is not simple immutability — it is *asymmetric* immutability. The same rule is unbreakable for one party and conditionally breakable for another. The party that would benefit from inflating supply (Grove, diluting its holders to fund itself) is denied the lever; the party that would suffer from Grove's insolvency (Sky, ultimately backing USDS) holds it.

The override's trigger is what makes it defensible rather than arbitrary: it is not a general Sky veto over Grove tokenomics, but a Risk-Framework-conditioned remedy available only when Grove has already breached its Risk Capital obligations. Emissions become a recapitalization tool of last resort, with dilution as the penalty for the breach.

The consequence for GROVE holders is that the supply cap is credible against the party most tempted to break it, while remaining explicitly *not* absolute. Anyone treating GROVE as a hard-capped asset is mispricing the tail risk that a Risk Capital violation forces dilution.
description: Asymmetric immutability: Grove Governance can never re-enable minting, while Sky Governance may force emissions when Grove violates Risk Capital requirements under the Risk Framework.
